title: Most Adults Cannot Pass This Social Worker Entrance Exam
summary: Explore thoughtful social work practice through clues, practical situations and fresh challenges.

landing.intro:
Listen, understand and reflect.
Choose a thoughtful next step.

about.body: Connect the facts, notice the details and test your understanding of thoughtful social work practice. Each checkpoint reveals your topic profile before a different challenge begins.

steps: Read the clues and choose one answer.
See your topic profile at each checkpoint and continue to a new challenge.
Reveal your overall result, then optionally review the answers you missed.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. This is not an accredited social-work admission, licensing or employment exam, and it is not professional or safeguarding advice. Laws, reporting duties and professional standards vary by location.

profile-1.copy: You answered almost every question correctly. Your breakdown shows how that accuracy carried across the topics in this challenge.

profile-2.title: Thoughtful Approach
profile-2.copy: You made many accurate connections across this challenge. Explore your breakdown to see which topics were strongest.

profile-3.title: Considered Perspective
profile-3.copy: You connected many of the clues and facts. Your breakdown highlights the topics you handled best and the ones worth another look.

profile-4.title: A Promising Start
profile-4.copy: You found useful clues across several topics. The answer review can help you work through the questions that caught you out.

profile-5.title: A First Look
profile-5.copy: Some topics were more familiar than others. Your review shows the correct answers and gives you a starting point for another attempt.

insights.overview: Your judgment score at a glance

socialworker-s1q1.question: Which question invites a person to describe an event in their own words?

answers.a2: “What happened next?”
answers.a4: “It happened exactly as I said, correct?”

socialworker-s1q2.question: Someone pauses while describing a difficult event. What is a useful response?

answers.a1: Ask several unrelated questions at once
answers.a2: Allow time and offer a calm opportunity to continue
answers.a3: Treat the pause as proof of dishonesty
answers.a4: Immediately fill in the missing details

answers.a1: Paying attention and checking your understanding
answers.a2: Planning your next speech while ignoring the answer
answers.a3: Speaking more loudly than the other person
answers.a4: Agreeing with every statement automatically

socialworker-s1q4.question: A term is unfamiliar to the listener. What helps?

answers.a2: Repeat more unexplained jargon
answers.a4: Explain it using clear, familiar words

socialworker-s1q5.question: Two people use the same word differently. What should be clarified?

answers.a1: What each person means by the word
answers.a2: Which person speaks faster
answers.a3: Nothing; identical words always mean identical ideas
answers.a4: Which word is longest

socialworker-s1q6.question: Which response checks understanding without assuming agreement?

answers.a2: “There is no need to explain further”
answers.a4: “I already know what you meant”

socialworker-s1q7.question: A language barrier affects an important discussion. What is the strongest support?

answers.a2: Using a child to translate sensitive details
answers.a4: Replacing every sentence with abbreviations

socialworker-s2q1.question: What does a strengths-based assessment look for alongside difficulties?

answers.a2: Only mistakes made in the past
answers.a4: A reason to ignore risks

socialworker-s2q2.question: Why ask the person what matters most to them?

answers.a1: Their goals and priorities help shape meaningful support
answers.a2: Their answer replaces every safety consideration
answers.a3: All people want the same outcome
answers.a4: Professionals never need other information

socialworker-s2q3.question: A family’s situation changes after an assessment. What may be needed?

answers.a1: A review of needs and support
answers.a2: Deletion of the earlier assessment
answers.a3: A conclusion based only on the family name
answers.a4: Automatic use of the old plan forever

socialworker-s2q4.question: What does considering the social environment add to an assessment?

answers.a1: Proof that individual preferences never matter
answers.a2: Context such as housing, relationships and available resources
answers.a4: Only a person’s eye colour

socialworker-s2q5.question: Which goal is specific enough to review?

answers.a1: “Confirm an appointment with the housing service by Friday”
answers.a2: “Improve without any agreed action”
answers.a4: “Make everything better someday”

socialworker-s2q6.question: A referral is made to another service. What helps continuity?

answers.a2: Closing all communication immediately
answers.a3: Clear relevant information, consent where required and an agreed follow-up process
answers.a4: Sharing every private detail regardless of relevance

socialworker-s2q7.question: Why distinguish an unmet need from an unwillingness to accept one particular option?

answers.a1: A person may need support but prefer a different appropriate approach
answers.a2: Everyone must prefer the first option offered
answers.a4: Refusing one option proves no need exists

socialworker-s3q1.question: A decision affects a close friend. What should a professional recognise?

answers.a1: A reason to hide the relationship
answers.a2: A guarantee of impartiality
answers.a4: An automatic exemption from procedure

socialworker-s3q2.question: Which approach treats comparable cases fairly?

answers.a2: Change criteria after seeing each person’s name
answers.a3: Use appearance as the only criterion
answers.a4: Apply relevant criteria consistently and consider relevant differences

socialworker-s3q3.question: A private record is useful for a task. What should determine access?

answers.a2: Authorised purpose and applicable access rules
answers.a3: Whether the file is easy to open
answers.a4: Whether the person is well known

socialworker-s3q4.question: You discover an error in your own report. What supports accountability?

answers.a2: Leave it because nobody has noticed
answers.a4: Correct it transparently through the appropriate process

socialworker-s3q5.question: What does informed agreement require in a meaningful discussion?

answers.a1: A promise that questions are forbidden
answers.a2: A decision made by an unrelated observer
answers.a3: Relevant information and an opportunity to understand and choose
answers.a4: A signature without any explanation

socialworker-s3q6.question: A gift could influence a professional decision. What is the appropriate response?

answers.a2: Hide the gift from the record
answers.a3: Follow the conflict-of-interest and gifts policy
answers.a4: Promise favourable treatment

socialworker-s3q7.question: A rule applies to everyone in a process. A popular person asks for a private exception. What is appropriate?

answers.a1: Grant it without recording the reason
answers.a2: Use the authorised process for any exception
answers.a4: Change the rule only for that person without explanation

socialworker-s4q1.question: Someone discloses possible harm. What is an appropriate first response?

answers.a2: Promise absolute secrecy regardless of risk
answers.a4: Listen calmly and take the concern seriously

socialworker-s4q2.question: Why explain the limits of confidentiality clearly?

answers.a2: All private information should be public
answers.a3: Some concerns may require appropriate information sharing
answers.a4: It removes every need for professional judgement

socialworker-s4q3.question: A concern may involve immediate danger. What should guide the response?

answers.a1: Urgency, safety and the relevant safeguarding procedure
answers.a2: Whether the report is convenient
answers.a3: Only the date of the next routine meeting
answers.a4: A promise to keep every detail secret

socialworker-s4q4.question: What should a record of a disclosure distinguish?

answers.a2: Only the writer’s preferred conclusion
answers.a4: The person’s words, observations and professional interpretation

socialworker-s4q5.question: A professional is unsure how to handle a safeguarding concern. What is appropriate?

answers.a2: Discuss identifying details casually in public
answers.a4: Seek prompt guidance through the designated process

socialworker-s4q6.question: Why avoid repeated leading questions after a disclosure?

answers.a2: More pressure always improves accuracy
answers.a3: They may influence the account and cause additional distress
answers.a4: The person’s words are never useful

socialworker-s4q7.question: A person needs protection and also has views about their support. What should the process consider?

answers.a2: Only professional convenience
answers.a3: The assumption that protection removes all voice
answers.a4: Both safety needs and the person’s participation as appropriate

socialworker-s5q1.question: Two people give different times for the same event. What is the best next step?

answers.a1: Average the times and call that a fact
answers.a2: Check each account against other reliable information
answers.a3: Choose the more confident speaker automatically
answers.a4: Delete both accounts without checking

socialworker-s5q2.question: Which statement records an observation rather than an assumption about motive?

answers.a1: The person never cared about the meeting
answers.a2: The person left because they were guilty
answers.a3: The person left the room at 14:10
answers.a4: The person intended to mislead everyone

socialworker-s5q3.question: A photograph has no known date or location. What should be checked before relying on it?

answers.a2: Whether its colours are attractive
answers.a4: Whether it matches a preferred conclusion

socialworker-s5q4.question: A claim is repeated by three websites, all quoting one unnamed source. What does that show?

answers.a1: Proof that no further checking is needed
answers.a2: Proof that the claim is accurate
answers.a4: Repeated reporting, not three independent confirmations

socialworker-s5q5.question: All authorised visitors have a pass. Mira has a pass. What follows from that rule alone?

answers.a1: Mira must be an authorised visitor
answers.a2: Mira cannot be an authorised visitor
answers.a4: It does not prove Mira is an authorised visitor

socialworker-s5q6.question: A new reliable fact contradicts your initial explanation. What is the sound response?

answers.a2: Change the fact to fit the explanation
answers.a3: Treat your first idea as unchangeable
answers.a4: Reconsider the explanation

socialworker-s5q7.question: A report says an event happened after a change. Does that timing alone prove the change caused it?

answers.a1: Yes; if the report is long enough
answers.a2: Yes; sequence always proves cause
answers.a4: No; earlier events can never cause later ones

socialworker-s6q1.question: Two records describe the same event but give different dates. What should be done?

answers.a1: Check the discrepancy against reliable original information
answers.a2: Average the dates and treat that as verified
answers.a4: Choose the later date automatically

socialworker-s6q2.question: Which note separates a statement from a verified fact?

answers.a1: “Lee reports that the door was open; this has not yet been checked”
answers.a2: “The door was certainly open because Lee said so”
answers.a4: “No check is needed because the story is detailed”

answers.a1: To remove the need for dates
answers.a2: So its source can be assessed and followed up
answers.a3: To make all information automatically true
answers.a4: To prove every source is independent

socialworker-s6q4.question: A document is a draft. What does that mean?

answers.a2: It may still change before being finalised
answers.a3: Every statement has been legally certified
answers.a4: It is necessarily false

socialworker-s6q5.question: A file has been revised several times. What helps identify the current version?

answers.a2: The longest filename alone
answers.a3: Whichever copy is easiest to find
answers.a4: A clear version and approval record

socialworker-s6q6.question: An entry is missing from a record. What does that establish by itself?

answers.a2: The information is not recorded there
answers.a4: The event definitely did not happen

socialworker-s6q7.question: Why preserve an original record when making an authorised correction?

answers.a2: To guarantee the original was correct
answers.a3: To make the record harder to understand
answers.a4: To prevent anyone seeing the correction

socialworker-s7q1.question: What is a professional boundary intended to protect?

answers.a1: The purpose and integrity of the helping relationship
answers.a2: The professional’s ability to avoid all questions
answers.a3: The right to ignore the person’s goals
answers.a4: A guarantee that no emotions are involved

socialworker-s7q2.question: A client sends a request through a personal social media account. What should guide the response?

answers.a1: A public discussion of the case
answers.a2: The service’s communication and boundary policy
answers.a3: An unrecorded promise of special access
answers.a4: A private friendship agreement

socialworker-s7q3.question: A practitioner is emotionally affected by a difficult case. What can support sound practice?

answers.a2: Making every decision alone to prove strength
answers.a4: Pretending the impact cannot exist

socialworker-s7q4.question: Why use the minimum relevant personal information when sharing a case?

answers.a1: To make the case impossible to understand
answers.a2: To hide relevant safety concerns
answers.a4: To support the purpose while limiting unnecessary disclosure

socialworker-s7q5.question: A person asks for help outside the practitioner’s competence. What is appropriate?

answers.a1: Use another client’s plan without assessment
answers.a2: Explain the limit and seek suitable support or referral
answers.a4: Invent expertise

answers.a1: Examining decisions, assumptions and their effects
answers.a2: Assuming every past choice was perfect
answers.a4: Replacing evidence with self-confidence

socialworker-s7q7.question: Why agree how and when support will be reviewed?

answers.a1: So the person need not be involved
answers.a2: So every goal is automatically achieved
answers.a3: So the plan can never change
answers.a4: So progress and changing needs can be considered

socialworker-s8q1.question: A supply box holds 24 items. Six are used. What fraction remains?

answers.a2: Three quarters
answers.a4: One third

socialworker-s8q2.question: A task begins at 14:35 and lasts 50 minutes. When does it finish?

socialworker-s8q3.question: Four equal groups share 36 items. How many items are in each group?

socialworker-s8q4.question: A reading rises from 40 to 50. What is the percentage increase?

socialworker-s8q5.question: A plan uses a scale of 1 cm to 2 m. What distance does 6 cm represent?

socialworker-s8q6.question: Three loads weigh 12 kg, 15 kg and 18 kg. What is their total mass?

answers.a2: 45 kg
answers.a4: 48 kg

socialworker-s8q7.question: A checklist has 20 items. Four remain unchecked. What percentage is complete?

socialworker-s9q1.question: A rule says: only members may enter. Sam is not a member. What follows under that rule?

answers.a1: Sam may enter if the queue is short
answers.a2: Sam must be admitted first
answers.a4: The rule says nothing about Sam

socialworker-s9q2.question: Every approved application has a signature. This application has no signature. What follows?

answers.a1: It is not approved under the stated rule
answers.a2: It is automatically approved
answers.a4: All applications lack signatures

socialworker-s9q3.question: A service opens only on Monday, Wednesday and Friday. Which day is definitely excluded?

answers.a2: Friday
answers.a4: Tuesday

socialworker-s9q4.question: Either Room A or Room B is booked, but not both. Room A is booked. What follows?

answers.a2: Room B is also booked
answers.a4: The booking must be cancelled

socialworker-s9q5.question: A rule requires both a form and proof of identity. Only the form is present. What is missing?

answers.a1: A second copy of the form
answers.a2: Nothing; one requirement is enough
answers.a3: A document not mentioned in the rule
answers.a4: Proof of identity

socialworker-s9q6.question: A policy says every urgent request is reviewed today. This request was reviewed today. What can you conclude?

answers.a2: No urgent requests were reviewed
answers.a3: It may or may not have been urgent
answers.a4: It cannot have been urgent

socialworker-s9q7.question: Three meetings happen in order: Ana before Bo, and Bo before Cam. Who meets last?

answers.a2: Cam
answers.a4: Ana

socialworker-s10q1.question: A plan sets a goal but no way to check it. What is missing?

answers.a2: An unrelated deadline
answers.a4: A different page colour

socialworker-s10q2.question: A decision is based on an old assessment, and circumstances have changed. What is needed?

answers.a2: Automatic repetition of the old decision
answers.a3: A decision based on memory alone
answers.a4: A review using current information

socialworker-s10q3.question: What is a useful purpose of supervision or professional consultation?

answers.a2: To avoid responsibility for every action
answers.a3: To reflect on difficult decisions and improve practice
answers.a4: To guarantee nobody can make a mistake

socialworker-s10q4.question: A task needs expertise you do not have. What is the appropriate response?

answers.a1: Seek suitable advice or referral within the process
answers.a2: Pretend to have the qualification
answers.a4: Choose the fastest answer regardless of risk

socialworker-s10q5.question: Two team members believe the other will make a follow-up call. What needs to be agreed?

answers.a2: Nothing; one will eventually guess
answers.a3: Who is responsible and when the action is due
answers.a4: Only the title of the file

socialworker-s10q6.question: A solution worked once. Does that guarantee it will fit every future case?

answers.a2: Yes; one success establishes a universal rule
answers.a3: No; successful ideas can never be reused
answers.a4: Yes; if the solution is easy to remember

socialworker-s10q7.question: What makes feedback useful for improvement?

answers.a1: A personal insult with no example
answers.a2: Specific observations and a clear next step
answers.a3: A claim that change is impossible
answers.a4: Only a vague label
